function_question: How does nature fold big things into small spaces?

opening.text: There was a girl called Ines who loved being a scout. She could tie six knots and spot north from the stars.
Ines and her scout group practised for the big camp on top of Lookout Hill, where you can see the whole valley.
They tried to carry the camp tent up the hill, and it was far too big and heavy. "If only it could fold up small enough to fit in a pocket," Ines sighed.

card.problem: The tent is too big and heavy to carry up the hill
card.goal: Make a shelter that folds tiny and opens big
card.rules: It must fold at least 10 times smaller and open in one move

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Ines's scout tent is too heavy to carry up Lookout Hill. She needs a shelter that folds tiny and opens big. Can you help her? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some engineers already have a spark of an idea for folding things small. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature packs huge wings and petals into tiny buds and bodies. Tap each card to meet four master folders!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which fold will open the fastest? Get your stopwatch ready for the unfold speed-run!
guide.sketch: Time to draw your shelter folded and open, with every fold line marked!
guide.build_and_test: Build your shelter, measure it open and folded, and find out how many times smaller it gets!
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Change ONE fold and test again. Did it get smaller?
guide.ending: And ever since then, Ines's scouts carry a shelter folded like YOURS in a pocket, and it pops open on every hilltop!

quick_check.question: Ines's model shelter is 40 cm × 30 cm open, which is 1,200 cm². Folded, it's 10 cm × 6 cm, which is 60 cm². How many times smaller is it folded?
quick_check.right: Right! 1,200 ÷ 60 = 20. Her shelter folds 20 times smaller, double her goal!
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Divide the open area by the folded area: 1,200 ÷ 60.

clue_cards.name: Hornbeam leaf
clue_cards.trick: It grows folded into neat zigzag pleats, like a paper fan.
clue_cards.does: The pleats open together, so the leaf spreads out flat in one smooth move.

clue_cards.name: Ladybird
clue_cards.trick: It folds its big flying wings along special creases.
clue_cards.does: The folded wings tuck under its hard wing cases and unfold in a split second.

clue_cards.name: Poppy
clue_cards.trick: Its petals are squashed and crumpled inside a snug bud.
clue_cards.does: When the bud opens, the wrinkly petals smooth out into a big flower.

clue_cards.name: Bat
clue_cards.trick: Its wing is thin skin stretched over long finger bones.
clue_cards.does: It folds its fingers together and the wing shrinks like a closed umbrella.

predict.prompt: Folded on a pattern or squashed at random? Predict first!

items.label: A tissue stuffed in a pocket

predict.explain: Things folded on a pattern open in one move and fold back the same way every time. Things squashed at random end up wrinkled and hard to open neatly.
